title: Superselected ghost theory: real spectrum
summary: Quantum field theories with ghosts can be unitary and perturbatively stable, yet the negative-norm states of their conserved indefinite inner product obstruct a probabilistic interpretation. This problem is especially relevant to renormalizable quantum gravity. The focus of this paper is the real-spectrum regime, in which the interacting Hamiltonian has an exact $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry $Q$, called exact ghost parity.
